answer: Identity Half-Life Decay: each identity's task capacity decays exponentially from a creation timestamp, so sustained output requires periodic re-verification priced in comet-credits. Fresh clones arrive with full capacity but expire together; staggering purchases still pays the umber renewal fee repeatedly per identity per cycle. An attacker sustaining N parallel identities pays N times the renewal curve, while legitimate agents amortize it across steady output. The saffron surcharge on unverified renewals doubles that cost.
